language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hi, I'm Chip.
Hi. My name is Suyin. My family and I grow many different types of plants. We sell our plants at the local market.
I am in charge of keeping track of the number of plants that we grow and sell.
I use graphs to help me track this information. Graphs are very useful.
I use sector graphs, divided bar graphs, bar graphs, and line graphs to track the number of plants that I sell.
I also calculate the mean and the median as I track the growth of my plants.
Let's help Suyin interpret graphs and calculate their mean and median. This will be fun!

I need to calculate the average height and the median height of my ginger plants so that I can decide the right time to sell them at the market.
The "average" is also called the "mean." To calculate the mean, we add up all the numbers and then divide the total by how many numbers we added.
The median is the middle number in a sorted list of numbers. To determine the median, sort the numbers in order from lowest to highest and then find the middle number.
If you have an odd amount of numbers, then there will be just one middle number.
If you have an even amount of numbers, then there will be two middle numbers. In this case, add the two numbers together and divide by two.
That number will be the median. Can you calculate the mean and median for different sets of numbers?
